clue.text: Secret of breaking out without injury

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the letters of the two words burst free and regroup in a new order

explanation.surface: A secret escapes, and nobody gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' rearranges SECRETOF into the answer; 'out' looks like part of an escape story but belongs to the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape unharmed or unpunished, so the phrase means untouched by harm.

clue.text: Fellow hired a wreath

parts.note: a fellow is a chap, an informal word for a man
let means rented out, as a house is let or hired

explanation.surface: A man rents a floral wreath for some occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or circlet of flowers worn on the head, a kind of crown of leaves.

clue.text: In a difficult situation, use hose on grass …

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights, legwear
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble turns a garden hose on the lawn, with the dots leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' pretends to be a garden hose and 'grass' a lawn, but they are legwear and cannabis slang; 'In a' and 'use ... on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight spot is an idiom for being in trouble with little room to escape.

clue.text: … found in this jacket

parts.note: continuing from the previous clue's grass, the name of a cannabis cigarette is also the name of a short double-breasted sailor's coat

explanation.surface: The cannabis from the previous clue turns up stashed in someone's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie this to 3 down: the grass (cannabis) is rolled into a joint whose slang name is also a type of naval jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is both a thick double-breasted jacket worn by sailors and a slang term for a marijuana joint.

clue.text: Three people, in general, treat learner badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the preceding words are treated roughly and jumbled

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Three people generally mistreat a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IN, GENERAL, TREAT and L (learner) into the fifteen letters; 'in general' looks like a stock phrase but its words are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is a romantic entanglement of a couple plus a lover, so a trio of people.

clue.text: Crushed wood — it is used to make a desk

parts.note: wood pulp is timber mashed down, as for paper

explanation.surface: Wood pulp is used to manufacture a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is used to make' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpit is the raised stand or lectern from which a preacher addresses a church congregation.

clue.text: With cards, I can stop

parts.note: a pack is a full set of playing cards
a can is a tin, a metal food container

explanation.surface: A card player declares they can stop playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' poses as a verb but is the noun, a tin; 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack it in is a colloquial idiom for giving up or quitting an activity.

clue.text: Here's a donation

definitions.meaning: being here, attending, is to be in attendance at roll call
a donation is a gift given to someone

explanation.definitionFit: Present means in attendance, here; and a present is a gift given freely.

clue.text: Prize given to the right officer

parts.note: to prize something is to treasure it, value it highly

explanation.surface: An official receives a prize for being correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like a noun award but is the verb to value; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is an official of a society or company responsible for its funds.

clue.text: Chaffer gets horse in draw

indicators.note: in tells us the horse is placed inside the word for draw

parts.note: hale is an old verb meaning to drag or haul, to draw
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A bargainer acquires a horse in a raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like a lottery but is the verb, as in haul; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaffer is an old verb for bargaining over a price, just like bartering.

clue.text: An apology for a dance

definitions.meaning: a polite phrase begging pardon for an interruption
a ballroom dance in which partners may be claimed by others cutting in

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase begs pardon politely, and it also names a party dance where one can cut in on a couple.

clue.text: Board with a bird, one who's slovenly

parts.note: a slat is a thin narrow strip of wood, a board
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone untidy turns up holding a plank and a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is an old, derogatory word for a dirty, untidy woman.

clue.text: Young devils encircle the Spanish forces

indicators.note: encircle shows the young devils surrounding the Spanish article

parts.note: imps are small mischievous devils
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Little demons surround Spanish troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forces' looks like a noun, military troops, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge someone onward, to compel them.

clue.text: Measures ladder

definitions.meaning: actions taken to deal with something
a stepladder, often just called a pair of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Steps are actions taken towards a goal, and a set of steps is a folding ladder.

clue.text: Something worn by Jack Ketch?

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious English hangman of the 1600s, so he was literally someone who hanged people; the clue reads him as a garment wearer while really naming his job

explanation.surface: What did a famous executioner wear?
explanation.walkthrough: A suspender is a garter or sock-holder; read literally, it is one who suspends, as Jack Ketch, an English public executioner whose name became slang for the hangman, did.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a garment strap holding up stockings, and also, literally, one who hangs things up, as a hangman does.

clue.text: Possibly a man-eater, a girl a lot involved

indicators.note: involved suggests the words are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl is heavily involved with a predatory man-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges AGIRLALOT; 'man-eater' tempts a reading about a seductive woman, but here it means a reptile, and 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Some large crocodilians are known to kill and eat people, so this reptile is one example of a man-eater.

clue.text: Shy member of the family

definitions.meaning: a shy is a fairground stall where you throw things at a target, here a traditional British pub and fair game with a dummy head
a relative, a parent's sister with a common first name

explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally is a British throwing game at fairs, a coconut-shy style target, and could also be a relative named Sally.

clue.text: Marine creature has first to undergo a metamorphosis

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, so the letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sea animal must be the first to transform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to undergo a metamorphosis' rearranges HASFIRST; the biology word suits the marine creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This echinoderm, with five arms radiating out, lives on the seabed.

clue.text: Required by law to be almost a model politician

indicators.note: almost means the word for a model falls just short of its final letter

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted figure, a model of a person
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: To qualify as a near-perfect Conservative is a legal duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from STATUE to give STATU; 'model politician' looks like one phrase but splits; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory means fixed or imposed by an Act of Parliament, laid down in statute.

clue.text: Flavouring also I perceive in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the phrase for perceiving goes inside the word for also

parts.note: and means also, in addition
I see means I perceive or understand

explanation.surface: A flavour is also noticed in the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts ISEE inside AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed, the seed of the anise plant, gives a liquorice taste to sweets and drinks.

clue.text: 20 moving out of range

indicators.note: moving out of suggests the letters of range are shifted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A feeling shifts beyond reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 20 down, a feeling; 'moving out of' rearranges RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is one particular strong feeling, an example of the general term at 20 down.

clue.text: Rising best-seller is a sensation

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the words for the best-seller are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a best-seller is a number one book, written NO 1 (with I for one) plus tome, a big book

explanation.surface: A book climbing the charts causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: A best-seller is a NO. 1 TOME, with I for the numeral one; 'Rising' turns NOITOME upwards; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling, like joy or fear, is something sensed and felt.

clue.text: Like 5, left amongst the rubbish

indicators.note: amongst places the letter for left inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: tripe is slang for nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Something is left among the garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is a triangle of three people, so 'Like 5' means threefold.
explanation.definitionFit: The trio in 5 down makes it threefold, made of three parts.

clue.text: What Cockney wife-beater does, we hear — this'll cure him

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer is something spoken rather than spelled

parts.note: a Cockney drops his aitches, so 'he licks her', meaning he beats her, comes out as 'e licks 'er

explanation.surface: A violent London husband needs a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: To lick is old slang for to thrash; a Cockney (a working-class Londoner) saying 'he licks her' drops the h sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a magical potion supposed to cure all ills or prolong life.

clue.text: Before being worn, a garment is returned, showing slight damage

indicators.note: Before here says the following pieces come ahead of the words for being worn

parts.note: a bra is a woman's undergarment

indicators.note: returned means the word is is read backwards

parts.note: something being worn is on, as clothes are on

explanation.surface: A bra comes back to the shop showing slight wear and tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IS into SI; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a graze or scrape, a minor wound to the skin or a surface.

clue.text: Home of the retiring bluefish

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for blue is read backwards

parts.note: blue means smutty or indecent, like lewd
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: The habitat of a shy bluefish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns LEWD into DWEL; 'bluefish' looks like the fish species but splits; 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or place to live.

clue.text: In bed I will turn pale

indicators.note: In places the contraction for I will inside the word for bed

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's bed or flat

indicators.note: turn says the contraction for I will is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Lying in bed, someone expects to go white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses I'LL to LLI, which 'In' puts inside PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means wan or lacking colour, as of a sickly face.

clue.text: Artist given food, a bit of salad

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a dish is a prepared plate of food

explanation.surface: A painter is served a meal, including some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a small red root vegetable often sliced into salads.

clue.text: Always over there, English people

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
yon is an old or dialect word for that, over there

explanation.surface: Forever over yonder, the English folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody, all persons collectively.
